image: sha256:d6ffd842978849651e756ebd39e9bf2da7ddb03e746113013533029878485a24 (spark-ds41f:candidate-48), changed files bind-mounted read-only; no image built
mark: keep the passing probe checks (boundary matrix 1404/1404, spec-decode 60/60, 0 LRU inversions) and the PR's 23-file test list, and bring the 64K-100K stress-probe overall hit share to at least 1107's on tp3 (retention 512) and tp4 (retention 8192), on two boots
reason: Root cause: 0763 re-appended every retained SWA checkpoint of a matched prefix to the MRU end on each hit, each window advance and each free, and re-sorted a finished request's already-free checkpoints into one tail-to-root run. A sliding-window hit reads only the window at the hit, so those aged checkpoints were the pool's harmless first eviction victims in 1107. Moving them behind the live conversation tails made pool pressure evict a conversation's newest positions first. The reworked 0763 removes that refresh. It keeps the decode-frontier retention, the stopping-step caching and the cross-group tail-to-root order of a freed request's own blocks. Every turn, evicted or not, now hits its last 256-token boundary: stress 99.8574% on tp3 and tp4, above 1107 (99.6759%, 99.5397%) and above candidate-48 (99.3809%, 98.9723%), identical on both boots. It misses one clause: the probe counts 6 LRU inversions per retention, not 0. That clause cannot be met together with the stress clause on this probe. Zero inversions means a conversation's cached blocks form one non-increasing run, so the probe's 18-block eviction must take agent 0's newest positions. That costs at least 1,536 tokens on turn 4 against a total tp3 margin over 1107 of 2,048 tokens for three evictions. The 6 inversions all sit between aged checkpoints, none inside a freed request's own run (diag/diag-lru-rework.txt). The live multi-turn hit-share part of the README mark still needs live serving and is not evaluated on sp8.
